submitter: static_site_form_endpoint thread, 2026-09-03 — round 1, migration 756 (storage half only; the Go receiver and the render-seam branch are separate coherent tasks and will take their own rounds)
rationale:
Every contact form this estate builds delivers by mailto: or not at all, and the owner has asked for a real endpoint so copyonline.co.uk's lead route reaches a human. This submission is ONLY the storage: two tables, no reader, no writer, nothing enabled. I am submitting the schema on its own and ahead of its consumers deliberately, because the schema is the part that is expensive to change once rows exist, and reviewing it after the handler is written means reviewing it after it is load-bearing.

What makes this worth a round rather than a rubber stamp is one design choice and one refusal. The choice: form_submissions.site_id is ON DELETE RESTRICT while route_id is ON DELETE SET NULL. A submission is a lead — possibly one someone paid for — and it is the only copy, because the design stores before it notifies; bugs_open/432 records that site rows do get deleted on this estate, so CASCADE would make a site deletion silently destroy them. Routing config, by contrast, must be re-pointable without touching the submissions it already produced. The refusal: I did NOT put the recipient address in the page or in sites.email. bugs_open/420's class fix has just separated delivery-contact from published-contact on that column, and adding a third meaning to it is exactly what that fix was undoing; the recipient lives here, per site AND per intent, read at delivery time so it can move without a rebuild.

The opt-in shape is the owner's 2026-08-02 §2 ruling applied literally: enabled defaults to FALSE, so a row alone does nothing, and the unsafe side is the default rather than a comment telling a future reader to be careful.

I want the reviewers to push on two things specifically. (1) Whether RESTRICT is right, or whether it will simply mean a future site-deletion job is written with a DELETE FROM form_submissions in front of it, achieving CASCADE with extra steps. (2) Whether intent as free text with a CHECK on its shape is the right extensibility axis, or whether it should be an enum/lookup — copyonline needs two intents on day one (commercial enquiry, directory removal request) and I have deliberately not constrained the vocabulary.

plan.summary: Migration 756: create site_form_routes (per-site, per-intent opt-in switch + movable recipient + the token the receiver resolves identity from) and form_submissions (the durable record, with notification bookkeeping). DB only, inert — nothing in the tree references either table name. Applied and verified 2026-09-03; committed with this submission.

edits.rationale: One table carries both the opt-in and the routing, because splitting them would let a site be enabled with no recipient. enabled defaults FALSE so the unsafe side is the default (owner 2026-08-02 §2). token defaults to encode(gen_random_bytes(32),'hex') and is UNIQUE with a length floor: it is what the receiver resolves the site from, because the existing tools-api middleware derives site identity from the Origin header, which an attacker sets freely — tolerable for a rate-limit bucket, not for an endpoint that emails a recipient. UNIQUE (site_id, intent) so two routes cannot claim one form.
edits.sketch:
CREATE TABLE site_form_routes (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  site_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES sites(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  intent text NOT NULL,
  token text NOT NULL DEFAULT encode(gen_random_bytes(32),'hex'),
  recipient_email text NOT NULL,
  reply_to text,
  enabled boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  CONSTRAINT site_form_routes_site_intent_uniq UNIQUE (site_id, intent),
  CONSTRAINT site_form_routes_token_uniq UNIQUE (token),
  CONSTRAINT site_form_routes_token_len CHECK (length(token) >= 32),
  CONSTRAINT site_form_routes_intent_shape CHECK (intent ~ '^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,39}$'),
  CONSTRAINT site_form_routes_recipient_shape CHECK (position('@' in recipient_email) > 1)
);

edits.rationale: The durable record, written BEFORE any notification is attempted. payload is jsonb because copyonline's payload is what-needs-writing / audience / tone / deadline / budget band, not a name-email-message triple, and the next customer's will differ again. intent is denormalised alongside route_id so a submission stays self-describing after its route is re-pointed or retired. ip_hash not ip: the estate's existing intake handler hashes (handlers/gripper.go hashIP), and storing raw addresses would build a personal-data store nobody asked for. notified_at / notify_attempts / notify_error exist so a failed send is a queryable row rather than a log line — a silently-dropping channel is the exact defect this lane exists to end.
edits.sketch:
CREATE TABLE form_submissions (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  site_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES sites(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  route_id uuid REFERENCES site_form_routes(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  intent text NOT NULL,
  payload jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  ip_hash text,
  user_agent text,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  notified_at timestamptz,
  notify_attempts integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  notify_error text,
  CONSTRAINT form_submissions_intent_shape CHECK (intent ~ '^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,39}$'),
  CONSTRAINT form_submissions_attempts_nonneg CHECK (notify_attempts >= 0)
);
CREATE INDEX idx_form_submissions_site_created ON form_submissions (site_id, created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX idx_form_submissions_undelivered ON form_submissions (created_at) WHERE notified_at IS NULL;
CREATE INDEX idx_site_form_routes_enabled ON site_form_routes (site_id) WHERE enabled;

edits.rationale: DO/RAISE rather than a block of SELECTs, because ON_ERROR_STOP ignores a non-empty result set and a SELECT-based verify cannot stop the COMMIT (RFC_006's landmine). Every assertion is paired with an induced failure so it cannot pass vacuously, and all three were proven to FAIL under mutation before I applied it — flipping the enabled default to true, changing the site FK to CASCADE, and deleting the token length CHECK each produced the intended refusal. The one place I deliberately did NOT induce is deleting a real sites row: sites carries a BEFORE INSERT trigger and a fan of CASCADEing dependents, so a delete that did not refuse would cascade across a live site before the RAISE rolled it back. That half is split into a behavioural check (insert a submission with a non-existent site_id, require foreign_key_violation, touching no real row) and a declarative one (pg_constraint.confdeltype = 'r'), and the file says plainly which is which.

The rollback REFUSES while form_submissions holds any row. Dropping real leads is not a rollback, it is data loss with a tidy name, and this table is their only store. Route rows do not block — they are regenerable config. A consequence worth stating rather than hiding: tokens die with the table, so any form markup already stamped with an old token stops working until the site re-renders. That is the correct failure direction — a stale token should be refused, not silently match a newly minted row.

grounded_in: MEASURED 2026-09-03, the SERVED layer, not content_data: of 27 contact-form components, 21 serve a real mailto: and 6 (on 6 sites) still serve '#contact'. Query: SELECT COALESCE(substring(rendered_html from 'action="([^"]*)"'),'(none)'), count(*), count(DISTINCT p.site_id) FROM page_components pc JOIN pages p ON pc.page_id=p.id WHERE pc.rendered_html ~* 'data-component="contact-form"' GROUP BY 1. The 6 are exactly the sites with an empty sites.email — boxingonline.com, cv1.co.uk, farmerinsurance.uk, garden-tools.uk, relojistas.com, plus the pool-ai-agents.internal pool row.

MEASURED 2026-09-03: the pre-plan's own census read content_data and reported 22 (now 27) dead forms, i.e. ALL of them. That figure is one layer above the repair — deliverableFormAction (platform/orchestration/actions/component_library.go:1495) rewrites a non-delivering action to mailto:<sites.email> at render. Recorded as a wrong call in WRONG_CALLS.md.

component_library.go:1456-1465, the existing seam's own statement of what it will not do: 'It deliberately does NOT fall back to a synthesised "info@<domain>" ... An address nobody reads makes the form look repaired while still losing the message, which is worse than the visible breakage: the failure stops being detectable from outside.' The endpoint is the destination that function has had no way to name.

internal/tools-api/store/sites.go:34, the reason identity is a token here and not the Origin header: `SELECT id, domain FROM sites WHERE status = 'deployed' AND domain = $1` — the domain comes from url.Parse(c.GetHeader("Origin")) in middleware/cors.go:16-17. A client sets Origin freely.

bugs_open/420 class fix, committed 162877051, the owner's ruling verbatim: 'When a customer pays but is never explicitly asked what contact details the site should show, the site publishes NONE. The payer's address is used only to deliver.' That fix separated delivery-contact from published-contact on sites.email; putting a form recipient on the same column would add a third meaning to the column it had just been rescued from.

bugs_open/432_HANDOFF_2026-09-02_a_site_whose_db_rows_were_deleted_keeps_serving_and_no_detector_can_enumerate_it.md — site rows DO get deleted on this estate. That is the evidence behind ON DELETE RESTRICT rather than CASCADE on form_submissions.site_id.

bugs_open/228_HANDOFF_2026-08-08 — a live component ('contact-block', 2 live pages incl. robot-hands.com's contact page) prints 'Your message has been sent. We'll be in touch shortly.' from a setTimeout, with no action, no method and no transport anywhere in its JS. Its ranked fix candidate 1 is 'Give the form a real destination and delete the timer', which is what this schema is the storage for.

MEASURED 2026-09-03, applied and verified at the DB rather than at the runner's report: SELECT to_regclass('public.site_form_routes'), to_regclass('public.form_submissions') → both non-null; route_rows 0, submission_rows 0 (no probe fixtures left behind); information_schema.columns shows enabled column_default 'false' and token default encode(gen_random_bytes(32),'hex'::text).

MEASURED 2026-09-03, blast radius stated as a query rather than an argument: no file in the tree references either table name. `grep -rn 'form_submissions\|site_form_routes' --include='*.go' --include='*.py' --include='*.sh' .` returns only migration 756 itself. There is no reader and no writer, so this migration cannot change any running behaviour.

MEASURED 2026-09-03, mutation testing of the verify block, each run through the migration runner's own doomed-transaction probe: (1) enabled DEFAULT true → 'verify: enabled did not default to false — the opt-in default is the wrong way round'; (2) site FK RESTRICT→CASCADE → 'verify: form_submissions -> sites is not ON DELETE RESTRICT — deleting a site could destroy leads'; (3) token length CHECK deleted → 'verify: the token length CHECK did not fire — constraint is inert'. All three killed, so none of the three assertions is vacuous.

CLAUDE.md owner ruling 2026-08-02 §2: 'New authority on a shared seam ships as an OPT-IN FIELD, not a documented contract ... when a seam's widest branch is licensed by "callers must all be X", make X a field with the unsafe default OFF ... A comment is not a control on a tree this many sessions share.' site_form_routes.enabled defaults false for exactly this reason.

CONTRIB_2026-09-03 from portfolio_positioning, the requirement that shaped the routing table: 'The recipient is expected to CHANGE without the page changing. Initially the site owner; later possibly a named third party who buys the leads. Whatever you build should let the destination move without a rebuild — that is a routing concern, not a form concern, and it is the thing we would most like designed in rather than bolted on.' And, for the intent column: 'the endpoint likely needs to serve at least two intents from one site — a commercial enquiry and a removal/correction request — with different recipients and different urgency.'
plan.risks:
1) THE RESTRICT/CASCADE CHOICE MAY BE DEFEATED IN PRACTICE. RESTRICT protects leads from an incidental site deletion, but nothing stops a future cleanup job from deleting submissions first and then the site — CASCADE with extra steps. What RESTRICT buys is that the deletion has to be WRITTEN, and therefore reviewed, rather than inherited. I think that is worth it; I would rather a reviewer told me it is not.

2) INTENT IS FREE TEXT with only a shape CHECK. Two lanes could invent 'removal' and 'removal_request' for the same thing and neither would fail. I chose this over an enum because the extensibility axis is the point and copyonline's second intent arrived after the first was specified — but it is a real drift surface and the estate has been bitten by vocabulary drift before. A lookup table is the obvious alternative and I did not take it.

3) THE TOKEN IS A BEARER SECRET THAT WILL BE PUBLISHED IN PAGE MARKUP. Anyone who views source on a site's contact page can read it and post to the endpoint as that site. This is deliberate and I want it stated plainly rather than discovered later: the token's job is to stop a stranger submitting AS AN ARBITRARY OTHER SITE (which a forged Origin allows today), not to authenticate the visitor, which is impossible for a public form. Abuse by someone holding the site's own token is bounded by httpguard's banded limiter and intake gate in the phase 2 receiver, and by the fact that such a submission is indistinguishable from one made through the form anyway. If a reviewer thinks a published bearer token is the wrong shape even for that narrow job, that is the objection I most want to hear now, because it is cheap to change with zero rows and expensive later.

4) NO RETENTION POLICY. form_submissions accumulates personal data (name, email, whatever the site's form asks) with no expiry and no deletion path beyond the rollback's refusal. I have deliberately not invented one, because retention is a business/legal decision and inventing a default would be worse than the gap — but the gap is real, it is a UK GDPR surface, and it should be a named owner decision before the first real submission lands, not after.

5) STORAGE IS APPLIED AHEAD OF ITS CONSUMERS, so if the phase 2 receiver is never built these tables sit empty for ever. That is a tidiness cost, not a risk to anything running: nothing reads or writes them, measured above.
